## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Abhayattheragāthā* (Thag 1.98) is a short canonical poem belonging to the *Theragāthā* within the Pali *Khuddakanikāya* [SuttaCentral]. It preserves a single verse attributed to the elder (thera) Abhaya. The SuttaCentral database records nine modern translations in eight languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus identifies substantial internal Pali text reuse between Thag 1.98 and several canonical and paracanonical works [DharmaNexus]. Segments of the poem (§0.4–1.5) exhibit near-verbatim alignment with the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (specifically SN 35.95) and the *Mālukyaputtattheragāthā* (Thag 16.5) [DharmaNexus]. Further matches are found within both parts of the commentary (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*) and the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā* of the *Saṃyuttanikāya* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting the reporting threshold in Sanskrit, Tibetan, or Chinese are recorded in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
